newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ABB builds new Swiss chip plant.
newsitem.headline: ABB builds new Swiss chip plant.

text.p: Electrical engineering group ABB Asea Brown Boveri AG said it would invest some 90 million Swiss francs to build a second semiconductor factory at an existing site in Lenzburg, in northern Switzerland.
The plant will create around 200 new workplaces, ABB Switzerland said in a statement.

The new factory will enable ABB Semiconductors AG, which employs some 180 people, take a leap in technology and help it expand its leading role as a supplier of power semiconductors on the world market.
The new factory should be operational from autumn 1998 and produce complex semicondutors of the latest generation of type IGBT (Insulated Gate Bipolar Transistor).
The new semiconductors are electronic switches that can switch current on and off several hundred times per second at power levels of up to 1,800 ampere at a voltage of 4,500 volt.
The chips are used in the areas of rail, power transmission and industrial plants.
